shipped_row.boundary_rationale: מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה (oshb:Prov.20.5) and רָב אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא (oshb:Prov.20.6) run one shared construction: a bare man-noun, איש, stands ahead of the verse's own etnahta in both (word 5 of 8 in 20:5, word 5 of 9 in 20:6), and a waw-prefixed second instance of that noun, ואיש, answers it just past the caesura in both, opening the second colon in construct with an abstract quality noun — תבונה, "understanding," in 20:5 and אמונים, "faithfulness," in 20:6 — before both verses close on that second colon's own predicate, ידלנה in 20:5 and מי ימצא in 20:6. A word-bound sweep of this same-verse bare-plus-waw-prefixed doubling (whitespace-token equality against the consonantal skeleton) returns 2 of 915 verses book-wide, and both hits are the two verses of this span. The bare noun by itself, word-bound, is far more common (53 of 915 verses), and a contiguous-consonantal-substring sweep of the same bare form is wider still (87 of 915 verses); the paired, colon-symmetric doubling sets this pair apart from that wider background.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 20:5 and 20:6 as two unrelated proverbs was rejected: the bare-plus-waw doubling that opens each verse's second colon is not the ordinary recurrence of a common noun but a paired, colon-symmetric construction, and a word-bound sweep of that exact doubling returns 2 of 915 verses book-wide, both of them this pair, so the two verses read as one deliberately constructed unit; extending the span to include Prov.20.4 or Prov.20.7 was also rejected, since neither neighboring verse shares a skeleton content token with either member of the pair.
